note: Three axes: technical domain x role function x organizational context. A job title is an alias for a combination, and no axis produces a ranking. This file is the place to edit. Changes in ME_V3_2: the fourth axis of the screening scale moved from organizational use to failure and correction; the materials domain was renamed to include strength; the ownership scope of control, equipment, requirements and automation was narrowed to what mechanical engineers actually take on; and quality and reliability was added to the role functions, making eight.

J1.name: Problem definition
J1.question: Who decided what to work on?

J2.name: Requirements interpretation
J2.question: Did you turn the requirements into numbers and constraints?

J4.name: Methods and tools
J4.question: What did you use, and how did you do it?

J6.name: Comparison and verification
J6.question: What did you compare it against?

J7.name: Failure and correction
J7.question: How did you narrow down what went wrong?

J8.name: Organizational use
J8.question: Who used it, and for what?

S4.note: Screening scale. These are the four asked in BASIC. Organizational use is left out of screening because it puts undergraduates at a structural disadvantage: whether your work was used by an organization can only be answered if you had a place in one, so someone with only coursework and a capstone leaves that cell empty even if they made real judgments. Failure and correction can be answered from undergraduate projects and still separates participation from ownership just as well. Organizational use is asked only in the in-depth part.

S8.note: Full scale. STANDARD and above. Do not report the S4 denominator as S8. What the in-depth part newly opens are the four not in screening (problem definition, requirements interpretation, methods and tools, organizational use).

levels.L1: Exposed. Watched or reused what someone else did
levels.L3: Owned. Decided it myself, and the result was used

technical_domains.name: Mechanical and Product Design
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes shape, dimensions, material, tolerances and fastening

technical_domains.name: Structural and Durability Analysis
technical_domains.owns: Whether it breaks under load, how much it deforms, and how many cycles it survives

technical_domains.name: Thermal and Fluid Systems
technical_domains.owns: Where the heat goes, and how flow rate and pressure are matched

technical_domains.name: Dynamics, Vibration and Noise
technical_domains.owns: At which frequencies it shakes, and where the vibration travels

technical_domains.name: Actuation, Transmission and Motion Design
technical_domains.owns: Looks at load, inertia and friction, then chooses the actuator and transmission to produce the required motion

technical_domains.name: Materials, Strength and Failure
technical_domains.owns: Which material and treatment to use, and at what strength and why it failed

technical_domains.name: Testing and Measurement
technical_domains.owns: What to measure, how, and how to judge the result

technical_domains.name: Production and Process Engineering
technical_domains.owns: Which manufacturing method and conditions make repeatable production

technical_domains.name: Equipment and Facility Operation
technical_domains.owns: Keeps the equipment performing as it should, and brings it back when it stops
subareas: Condition diagnosis and root cause of failures

technical_domains.name: Quality and Reliability
technical_domains.owns: Whether the requirements hold through mass production and over the product's life

technical_domains.name: Requirements, Constraints and Schedule
technical_domains.owns: Breaks down requirements and constraints and ties them into a schedule and interfaces

technical_domains.name: Task Automation and Data
technical_domains.owns: Captures repeated calculations, data handling and pass/fail judgments so they can be reused

role_functions.name: Design and development
role_functions.success: One design that can be built and meets the requirements

role_functions.name: Analysis and prediction
role_functions.one_line: Knows the outcome before it is built
role_functions.success: Predictions that match tests and justify a design change

role_functions.name: Testing and verification
role_functions.one_line: Checks whether what was built is right
role_functions.success: A result whose verdict can be reproduced, with the uncertainty stated

role_functions.name: Process and mass production
role_functions.one_line: Makes it possible to build repeatedly
role_functions.success: Yield and takt time within target

role_functions.name: Integration and coordination
role_functions.one_line: Ties many people's decisions into one

role_functions.name: Exploration and research
role_functions.one_line: Narrows down things that have no answer yet
role_functions.success: The question is narrowed and a method remains

role_functions.name: Quality and Reliability
role_functions.one_line: Assures that requirements hold through mass production and over the product's life
role_functions.success: Defects do not recur and the basis for each decision can be traced

org_contexts.name: Finished-product company
org_contexts.differs: Receives requirements and does a lot of integration

org_contexts.name: Component, equipment or materials company
org_contexts.performance: Meeting customer specs, yield, unit price
org_contexts.differs: Goes deep in one area and passes customer validation

org_contexts.name: Engineering and technical services
org_contexts.performance: Deadlines, use in the client's decisions, repeat business
org_contexts.differs: Takes on someone else's problem, states its assumptions openly and delivers an answer

org_contexts.name: Government-funded research institute
org_contexts.differs: Project templates and interim reviews set the schedule

org_contexts.name: University and research lab
org_contexts.differs: Has to establish the validity of its own methods

org_contexts.name: Public sector, regulation and certification
org_contexts.performance: Judgments of compliance with standards, and their basis
org_contexts.differs: The traceability of the judgment is the output

org_contexts.name: Startup or small manufacturer
org_contexts.performance: A working product, launched before the money runs out
org_contexts.differs: One person takes on several roles at once

boundaries.shared: Both size parts based on loads and materials
boundaries.a_difference: Has the authority to change dimensions
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for the validity of the prediction
boundaries.a_question: Did that result change the dimensions on the drawing?
boundaries.b_question: Have you checked that result against hand calculations or tests?

boundaries.a_difference: Defines the functions to deliver when no specification exists
boundaries.b_difference: Delivers a design that meets a given specification
boundaries.a_question: Have you written the required specifications yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you released an approved drawing?

boundaries.shared: Both solve physics with commercial tools
boundaries.a_difference: Looks at loads, stresses and service life
boundaries.b_difference: Looks at heat loads, flow rates and pressures
boundaries.a_question: Have you calculated a fatigue life or a safety factor?
boundaries.b_question: Have you chosen a mesh and a turbulence model?

boundaries.pair: Structural analysis vs. vibration and NVH
boundaries.shared: Both look at how a structure behaves
boundaries.a_difference: Looks at static and fatigue loads
boundaries.b_difference: Looks at frequencies and transfer paths
boundaries.a_question: Have you found a stress concentration and reinforced it?
boundaries.b_question: Have you changed a design to avoid a resonant frequency?

boundaries.pair: Testing and measurement vs. quality and reliability
boundaries.shared: Both judge whether something meets a standard
boundaries.a_difference: Sets the verdict and the uncertainty for a single case
boundaries.b_difference: Checks that it holds through mass production and over the product's life
boundaries.a_question: Have you stated a measurement uncertainty?
boundaries.b_question: Have you calculated process capability or a life distribution?

boundaries.pair: Production and process engineering vs. equipment and maintenance
boundaries.a_difference: Controls quality and takt time through conditions and methods
boundaries.a_question: Have you changed machining conditions or a manufacturing method?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set a maintenance interval or a replacement criterion?

boundaries.pair: Materials and failure vs. quality and reliability
boundaries.shared: Both look at why something broke
boundaries.a_difference: Identifies the damage mechanism from the materials side
boundaries.b_difference: Separates occurrence from escape on the process side
boundaries.a_question: Have you examined a fracture surface or a microstructure?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set countermeasures separately for occurrence and escape?

boundaries.pair: Systems and requirements vs. technical PM
boundaries.shared: Both tie together many people's decisions
boundaries.a_difference: Breaks down requirements, allocates them and traces them
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for schedule, resources and changes
boundaries.a_question: Have you assigned a verification method to each requirement?
boundaries.b_question: Have you reworked a schedule and resources?

boundaries.b_difference: Finds trends and anomalies in the values
boundaries.a_question: Are other people doing their work with it?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set decision criteria as numbers?

boundaries.pair: Control and mechatronics vs. mechanical design
boundaries.a_question: Have you tuned a gain or a sequence?
boundaries.b_question: Have you decided a tolerance allocation?

boundaries.pair: Analysis and prediction vs. exploration and research
boundaries.shared: Both know the result before it is built
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for the validity of predictions on problems that have a specification
boundaries.b_difference: Establishes the method itself when there is no specification
boundaries.a_question: Have you checked that prediction against test values?
boundaries.b_question: Have you created a new method because no usable one existed?

boundaries.pair: Equipment and facility operation vs. production and process engineering
boundaries.shared: Results only come when the equipment runs
boundaries.a_difference: Keeps the equipment performing as it should, and brings it back when it stops
boundaries.b_difference: Decides what to make with that equipment and under which conditions
boundaries.a_question: Have you narrowed down the cause when equipment behaved abnormally?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set machining or molding conditions?

role_functions_note: There are eight. The boundaries were rewritten so that analysis and prediction and exploration and research do not refer to the same work: analysis and prediction is responsible for the validity of predictions on problems that have a specification, while exploration and research establishes the method itself when there is no specification. Quality and reliability was separated from testing and verification because a test judges a single case, while quality assures the whole of mass production and service life.
